key_insight: A semi-automated, expert-guided annotation pipeline can turn a small number of labeled intraoperative ultrasound frames into usable segmentation across full neurosurgical video sequences.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could reduce the time and expertise needed to build AI tools for real-time brain tumor and anatomy interpretation during surgery.
method: Napari-based interactive labeling interface for neurosurgical ultrasound videos
Random Forest pixel classifier trained on sparse expert brush annotations using intensity, multi-scale Gaussian, Laplacian of Gaussian, and Sobel features
Incremental multi-case training with OOB validation and exported TIFF overlays for review
evidence_signal: In five craniotomy cases, sparse annotations from a neurosurgical expert were sufficient to train case-specific models that propagated labels across full intraoperative ultrasound sequences, with OOB estimates and qualitative expert review used for assessment.
watch_item: This is a proof-of-concept study with only five cases and qualitative review, so broader accuracy, robustness, and generalizability remain unproven.
paper_title: A Semi-Automated Interactive Annotation Framework for Intraoperative Neurosurgical Ultrasound: A Proof-of-Concept Study
